Start here: what the audit found
Over 12 months the account spent ₦189.2M for 9,607 Meta-attributed purchases worth ₦1.19B (ROAS 6.28, CPA ₦19,695). The money is not the problem. The structure is.
• The account never leaves the learning phase. 476 campaigns were launched in 12 months, with a median life of 8 days. Of 2,742 ad-set-weeks, none reached 50 purchases.

• Proven winners get paused. 27 Sales ad sets that returned at least 9× are now paused. Examples: CEO Passion NG at 22.45, Passion & Seduction at 15.26, NG Catalogue at 12.05. Each was replaced by a fresh ad set that starts learning from zero.

• International spend is the largest drag. The UK, Canada and the US took 48.9% of spend (₦92.6M) at ROAS 3.58 and CPA ₦38,875. Nigeria returned 8.86 at CPA ₦13,364. Of the 149 Sales-objective ad sets that spent past the threshold with zero purchases, 145 were international.
Single primary bottleneck: fragmentation. Budget is spread across dozens of short-lived ad sets on ₦10,000–₦15,000 a day, none of which can gather the roughly 50 purchases a week that Meta needs.

Most critical recommendation: consolidate Nigeria into one or two long-running Sales campaigns, with a budget that can clear 50 purchases a week (about ₦95,000 a day per ad set at Nigeria's observed CPA). Feed new creative in as ads inside those campaigns, not as new campaigns.
Treat every efficiency figure below as an upper bound. In September 2026, Meta reported more purchases (861) than Shopify recorded in total (804).

• The structural findings hold regardless of measurement. These are fragmentation, churn, zero ad-set-weeks above 50, paused winners, and the market cost gap (CPM and CPA abroad are 3–8 times Nigeria's). They rest on spend, impressions and purchase counts.

Funnel Stage, Audience and Ad Format were therefore taken from Meta's own metadata and marked tier = metadata on every row:

• Null and zero can't be told apart for actions. The connector returns 0 rather than null when an action is missing.

PART A: LIVE ADS (112 ads · 55 ad sets · 54 campaigns)

Live means the ad's effective status is ACTIVE, which also requires its ad set and campaign to be active. Over 12 months these ads spent ₦13,777,957 (7.3% of the total). In the last 7 days (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-06) they spent ₦2,671,219.

Context that matters: 45 of the 55 live ad sets were launched between 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-06, so they are 1–5 days old. Together they have spent ₦1,676,905 for 32 purchases (ROAS 2.59). That is too early to judge. The other 10 live ad sets account for ₦12,101,052 of spend at ROAS 7.77.

• No live ad retargets anyone. Every live ad set targets cold audiences, with interests or broad targeting, and Advantage+ audience switched on. Meta's events show demand that has no dedicated follow-up: over 12 months they recorded 39,422 adds to cart and 44,233 checkouts initiated, against 9,607 purchases.
• Broad returns more than Interest on live spend (8.32 against 6.69). Most of the Broad figure comes from one ad set: Golden Kiss image - NG (₦3.53M, ROAS 8.78).
• With Advantage+ audience on, the two are not cleanly separated, so read this as a direction rather than proof.
• Static is the most efficient live format, but it holds only 15.3% of live spend.
• Video takes half of live spend and returns the least. Part of that is the market mix: most of the new UK, Canada and US launches are video.

• Check this: the "CA Awareness" campaign targets the UK, not Canada. All 5 of its live ads target GB, and it has spent ₦286,314 since 2026-09-09. Its sister campaign "UK Awareness" also targets the UK, so the two overlap and Canada gets no awareness at all. This looks like a setup error.

• The two Awareness campaigns (₦571,684, Reach-optimised, live since 2026-09-09) produce no purchases. That is expected for the Reach objective, so they are not waste on their own terms. Note, though, that they push awareness into markets returning ROAS of about 3.4–3.9.

PART B: OTHER ADS (1,301 ads · 601 ad sets · 424 campaigns, not live) and the 12-month account

These ads are no longer delivering, so they can't be paused. They matter because they show the pattern behind the live ads: what was tried, what worked, and what was switched off. The account totals below include the live ads.
B2. Funnel stage: 12 months, all ads
• Retargeting has effectively never been run. Two ad sets used warm custom audiences: "WEB 180Days" and "IG 365"/"IG AUDIENCE". Together they spent ₦161k for 1 purchase.
• There is no evidence that retargeting works or fails here. Z3 can't fire meaningfully on ₦161k, so this is an untested opportunity rather than a finding.
• Interest, Broad and Lookalike return within about 0.9 ROAS of each other. With Advantage+ audience on everywhere, audience choice is not what drives performance in this account. Market is.
• One Lookalike ad set, "lookalike Campaign" (Lookalike 5% of 180-day purchasers, Nigeria), returned 9.56 on ₦2.11M and is now paused.
• Catalogue is the most efficient format and the least funded. It ran on 6 ads (1.4% of spend), including "NG Catalogue" at ROAS 12.05 on 225 purchases, which is now paused.
• Static beats Video and Carousel on CPA. No format meets Z6 (at least 15% of spend at below half the account ROAS), so format alone isn't wasting money.

• The structural findings hold regardless of measurement. These are fragmentation, churn, zero ad-set-weeks above 50, paused winners, and the market cost gap (CPM and CPA abroad are 3–8 times Nigeria's). They rest on spend, impressions and purchase counts.
• All ROAS and CPA figures are Meta-attributed with view-through, so treat them as upper bounds.
– September 2026 is overstated by at least 7.1%.
– The 12-month share of 75.8% of all store orders looks high for an account that also runs Google Ads, with organic Instagram, direct and repeat buyers also contributing.

Ordered by size of opportunity. Every change below is a test to run. Nothing has been changed in the account.
[High priority 1] Consolidate Nigeria into long-running campaigns that can exit learning

• Hypothesis: Meta can't stabilise delivery on ad sets that get 5 purchases a week. Pooling Nigeria's budget into fewer ad sets, each with 50 or more purchases a week, will let delivery exit learning and lower CPA. In the live data, ad sets Meta marks SUCCESS returned ROAS 8.37 at CPA ₦16,405, against 2.83 and ₦51,941 for those still LEARNING. That comparison is confounded by age, so it is an indication rather than proof.

– Build one Nigeria Sales campaign (Advantage campaign budget, Purchase or Value optimisation) with 1–2 ad sets at about ₦95,000–₦100,000 a day each. That is well within what Nigeria already spends: ₦14.05M in September 2026 is about ₦468,000 a day.
– Seed it with the proven creative from the paused winners: CEO Passion NG, Passion & Seduction, Dimma, Amy okoli, NG Catalogue, Mini set Vid and Goddess DT/NG.
– Fold the live Nigeria ad sets into it: Golden Kiss image - NG, MGG NG-DT, Goddess DT/NG, Mystique NG-DT, 09 Mystique NG, Mystique NG- Broad and Golden kiss | NG | DT | Lagos.
– From then on, add new creative as ads in that campaign, not as new campaigns.
• Expected effect: each ad set clears 50 purchases a week within 2–3 weeks and leaves learning. CPA falls from the September 2026 Nigeria level (₦20,183) toward the 12-month Nigeria level (₦13,364).
• Measure: weekly purchases per ad set (target 50 or more), CPA and ROAS against the 4 weeks before the change, and Shopify orders against the same 4 weeks. Judge after 4 weeks.

• Worth: at September's Nigeria spend (₦14.05M, 696 purchases), a 15% cut in CPA (₦20,183 → ₦17,156) would mean about 123 more purchases a month, roughly ₦15.2M of attributed value at ₦123,620 each. This is an illustrative estimate; the real effect is what the measure decides.
[High priority 2] Re-test the market split with a measured shift from international to Nigeria

• Hypothesis: international purchases cost 2.9 times Nigerian ones (CPA ₦38,875 against ₦13,364) because CPMs abroad are 3–8 times higher. Moving part of the international budget to Nigeria buys more purchases per naira, unless international orders carry a margin the data can't see.
– Move 20% of the international budget to Nigeria, about ₦2.28M of the ₦11.40M that the UK, Canada and the US took in September 2026.

– Take it first from the ad sets that hit Z1 and from the October launches still at zero purchases after 7 days. From the live list: Mini set | CA | 23-45 | DT | Both, the Mystique, Sweet OUD and Goddess | CA | 10 | NID ad sets with no purchases, and the Golden Kiss | UK | 23-45 | Women | Broad pair.
– Keep the international ad sets that are returning, so the diaspora channel isn't switched off.

• Expected effect: at 12-month observed rates, ₦2.28M buys about 59 purchases abroad or about 171 in Nigeria. Nigeria's marginal ROAS is falling as its spend rises (December 2025: ₦1.41M at 34.05; September 2026: ₦14.05M at 6.72), so plan on the lower end.
• Measure: account purchases, Shopify orders and blended revenue ÷ Meta spend, over 4 weeks against the prior 4.
• Worth: up to about 112 more purchases a month at 12-month rates, roughly ₦13.8M of attributed value. Treat it as an upper bound.
[High priority 3] Stop pausing winners; refresh their creative instead

• Hypothesis: paused winners didn't stop working all at once; many fatigued gradually (Z7). Refreshing creative inside a winning ad set keeps its learning, whereas pausing it and relaunching restarts learning from zero.
– Set a rule. Before pausing an ad set with a 30-day ROAS of at least 1.5 times the account average (9.4 or more), add 2–3 new ads to it, and pause the fatigued ad only.
– Apply it now to the live Z12 ad sets: Goddess DT/NG, Mystique NG-DT and 09 Mystique NG, which are barely delivering at present.
– Apply it to Golden Kiss image - NG, where 3 ads fell to 0.00 ROAS in their last 30 days (Z7).
• Expected effect: fewer ad sets restart learning, so cost per purchase rises less after each creative change.
• Measure: count of ad sets kept past 30 days, and their ROAS in weeks 5–8 against weeks 1–4.
• Worth: the 28 paused Z12 ad sets returned ₦24.2M of spend at 9.4–22.5 ROAS, which shows these structures could be kept running.
[Medium priority] Fix the Awareness targeting and question the international Awareness spend
• Hypothesis: the "CA Awareness" campaign targets the UK, so Canada gets no awareness and the UK gets two overlapping Reach campaigns.

• Action: confirm the intended geography for CA Awareness (₦286,314 spent, ₦76,174 in the last 7 days, budget ₦10,000 a day). Then decide whether ₦20,000 a day of Reach in markets returning ROAS 3.4–3.9 earns its place.
• Expected effect: correct reach in Canada, or about ₦600,000 a month freed for Nigeria.
• Measure: CA reach and frequency; UK frequency. Judge over 2 weeks.
• Worth: about ₦600,000 a month of Reach spend.
[Medium priority] Launch a measured retargeting test

• Hypothesis: the 39,422 add-to-cart and 44,233 checkout-initiated events over 12 months, against 9,607 purchases, are a warm pool the account never targets. Retargeting it should convert at a lower CPA than cold Nigeria traffic.

• Action: one retargeting ad set per market cluster (Nigeria; UK, Canada and US), using website AddToCart and InitiateCheckout audiences from the last 30 days, excluding purchasers from the last 30 days, at about 10% of the market's budget. Fix the AddToCart event gap first (see Tracking).
• Expected effect: retargeting CPA below Nigeria's ₦13,364. Audience size decides whether this can scale.
• Measure: CPA and ROAS against prospecting, plus incremental Shopify orders, over 4 weeks.
• Worth: unknown. Retargeting has never been tested here (₦161,000 in 12 months), so the size of the opportunity can't be estimated yet.
[Creative or testing] Fund the formats that return: Catalogue and Static in Nigeria
• Hypothesis: Catalogue (ROAS 10.69, CPA ₦11,522) and Static (7.30, ₦16,618) beat Video (6.27, ₦19,589). In this account, the product image sells.
• Action: add a Nigeria catalogue (DPA) ad to the consolidated campaign, using the "NG Catalogue" product set, and run 2–3 static variants of the best-selling products.

• Worth: NG Catalogue alone returned ₦27.1M on ₦2.25M.
[Measurement before scaling anything] Reconcile Meta to Shopify
• Hypothesis: in September, Meta claimed 107% of all Shopify orders, so ROAS is overstated and some purchases may be double-counted.
